newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house fills up for civil service vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house fills up for civil service vote.

text.p: About 460 members of Brazil's Chamber of Deputies were registered as present in Congress, enough for the government to press ahead with a vote on its civil service reform bill later Wednesday, an official said.
"We're going to vote," said an aide to the government's chief whip in the lower house, Deputy Benito Gama.

The aide said the government had not bowed to pressure from members of allied political parties to exclude lawmakers and other categories of public sector workers from a proposed ceiling on pay and pensions.
The 10,800 real ($10,188) monthly ceiling proved the stumbling block in the government's failed attempt to put the civil service reform bill to a first vote in the Chamber of Deputies last month.
Lawmakers who stand to lose under the ceiling were expected to propose an amendment to exclude themselves from the pay cap. That amendment would be voted on after the reform bill itself.
The legislation is considered central to the government's efforts to cut public spending to narrow Brazil's public sector deficit.
It would enable states and municipalities that spend more than 60 percent of receipts on payrolls to dismiss currently unfireable workers.
The bill was sent to Congress in August 1995 and its progress has been snail-paced in the face of opposition ranging from trade unions to government-allied parties.
As a constitutional amendment, the bill requires two three-fifths majorities in the 513-member Chamber of Deputies and in the 81-member Senate.
